It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A Taunton man has been jailed for eight years and seven months for raping and repeatedly sexually abusing a child. Elijus Navickas, 24, admitted four offences including rape and assault of a child by penetration. The court heard the offending took place over a period of several years while the victim was aged between seven and 10. Sentencing him at Taunton Crown Court on Friday (August 7), His Honour Judge Cook said the abuse had left the victim "overwhelmed by her emotions". Judge Cook told the court of Navickas' abuse on the victim, including touching and oral penetration. He said: "She said she didn’t like what you were doing. "She was too scared to tell her mother because you were strong and an adult." The abuse came to light in 2025. Once Navickas was arrested, he made full admissions in the police interview. The court heard Navickas told the police the abuse happened around 20 to 40 times in total. It said: "I watched my daughter lose some of her confidence, it is hard to see her carrying emotions no child should have to carry. "Learning what happened [to my daughter] was one of the most traumatic experiences of my life. "The emotional impact on our family is profound and will remain with us for many years to come." Harry Adjuha, defending Navickas, said he "very much regrets what he did and is very sorry" for his actions. It was heard Navickas was born in Lithuania, and so Mr Adjuha said he knows there is a "strong likelihood he will be deported". In mitigation, he said Navickas was exposed to pornography from just nine years old, and Mr Adjuha noted this "may have" played a role in his attitude towards sex and boundaries. Judge Cook sentenced Navickas to eight years and seven months in prison. He also gave him a sexual harm prevention order and restraining order, both for life, and said he would have to comply with notification requirements for the rest of his life as well. https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Australia has broken into the top 10 of the World Economic Forum’s Global Gender Gap Report, ranking eighth out of 148 countries – its highest ranking ever. The 2026 report marks a significant climb for Australia, moving up 35 places from 43rd since the Albanese government took office. The government credits this historic high to improved political representation (including a majority-female cabinet), expanded paid parental leave, wage increases in female-dominated sectors and new investments in women’s health. Anthony Albanese said in a statement that the ranking “slipped to an all-time low of 50th under the previous Coalition government” and acknowledged that the work must continue: The job is not done and we will continue to focus our efforts on lifting wages, ending gender-based violence, increasing female representation in workplaces, investing in women’s health and more.
